{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.50) as it often signals downward pressure.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility after consecutive high peaks — model tends to overshoot and overreact to recent spikes.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5-10% to align with historical mean.",
    "Increase downward bias when sentiment shifts from neutral to negative, especially if true outcome has been trending lower.",
    "Avoid over-optimism in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5 days) — model often overestimates short-term rallies.",
    "If true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a 3-5% downward correction to future forecasts to account for model overconfidence.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.50 (positive sentiment), slightly increase forecast to reflect bullish momentum, but cap at 10% above recent high.",
    "Lag correction: if true outcome is 2-3 days behind forecast, adjust forecast downward by 2-5% to account for delayed market reaction."
  ]
}
